items.title: Harold Mabern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 31, 2010
items.q: I did one beautiful quartet date with Art Farmer called “Perception” with Roy McCurdy, Tommy Williams and myself.

ctx.x: I’m still single at the time, yeah. So then when I got with the Jazztet, that was, as a matter of fact there’s a book out now that was put out by the Baroness Rothschild called

Musicians’ Three Wishes. And she would go around with a camera and ask the musicians if they had three wishes what would that be. And come to find out I’m in the book. I never had no idea. I don’t even recall her or anybody talking to me. Because see here again, I would go to hear Thelonious Monk I would sit at the table with the band but I was well reserved and I knew how to keep my mouth shut and not speak until I was spoken to. And see even then, the older musicians liked me because I wasn’t one to run my…
Would that band have gone under the heading of hard bop?

items.title: Roy McCurdy interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: We used to work together a long time ago with Harold Mabern and Bob Cranshaw.

ctx.x: She’s really I think one of the truest of jazz singers.
Yeah, she could sing. We used to work together a long time ago with Harold Mabern and Bob Cranshaw.
